name: Op Art Illusion
summary: Riley and Vasarely optical art: healthy data is a perfect pattern, the anomaly is a coral warp your eye catches first.
look: Ink stripes and checkerboards on warm paper, teal concentric rings, one coral compression zone. Type always sits on thick ink-bordered paper cards to stay readable.

components.name: Riley wave field
components.role: 52 sine-modulated ink stripes, 11 px, as visual overload

components.name: Vasarely tunnel
components.role: offset concentric teal/paper rings that pull toward the mark

components.name: Checker field
components.role: regular squares standing for healthy metrics

components.name: Warp zone
components.role: column compression where squares turn coral — the anomaly

components.name: Ink-bordered card
components.role: 8 px ink frame holding type calmly on top of the pattern

components.name: Calm stripes
components.role: evenly spaced teal bars for the resolved end state

motion.name: Phase shimmer
motion.how: wave phase += 0.35 rad per 8th note, stepped (no easing) so the vibration locks to 120 BPM

motion.name: Warp squeeze
motion.how: column widths animate to the Gaussian compression, sine.inOut 1 s (2 beats); relax with elastic.out after the human clicks

motion.name: Tunnel pull
motion.how: ring scale 1→1.25 with expo.in 0.5 s into the drop, then hard cut to the settled frame

story: Hook: an overwhelming field of Riley-style wavy stripes behind "How many dashboards did you check today?". Reveal: stripes collapse into a teal Vasarely tunnel with the Acme mark at its centre. Proof: a calm checkerboard squeezes into a coral warp; the card shows checkout conversion −18% since 09:42, deploy #2231, Roll back / Acknowledge. CTA: stripes straighten, "Every metric. Every minute." with Start free.
adapt: Use the regular pattern for 'normal' in your domain (requests, transactions, builds) and warp it where your product catches something. Replace the evidence card with your own alert UI.

references.note: optical-art techniques: line vibration, figure-ground, colour contrast

fit.risk: Moiré and flicker after compression; possible visual discomfort — keep patterns coarse and slow.
